sentences.text: Rinconraptor represents a newly named genus and species of megaraptorid theropod dinosaur.
The animal is estimated to have reached about 7 metres in length, placing it within the medium-to-large size range for members of its clade.

Its forearm and lower-leg bones display a distinctive mix of features, such as a separated ectepicondyle on the humerus, a straight lateral margin of the tibia, and a subrectangular cnemial crest together with a medial condyle.
Additional traits include an anterodistally-oriented ridge on the humerus and a right-angled incisura tibialis, conditions previously known only from Megaraptor and Fukuiraptor respectively.
The genus and species were formally described by Ariel H. Méndez and colleagues in 2026.
The sediments preserving Rinconraptor indicate fluvial and aeolian systems within a semi-arid paleoenvironment.

It shared its ecosystem with other theropods such as the megaraptorid Tratayenia, the abelisauroids Velocisaurus, Llukalkan and Viavenator, alvarezsaurids Achillesaurus and Alvarezsaurus, the unenlagiine Diuqin, and the avialans Neuquenornis and Patagopteryx.
Only a single fossil occurrence of Rinconraptor has been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.
Rinconraptor lived during the Late Cretaceous Santonian age in the Bajo de la Carpa Formation of Argentina.
The Santonian stage spans roughly from 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago.
